beats.intro: Learning module nine. [[sub]]Put-call parity: how calls, puts, the underlying and a bond fit together.
beats.portfolios: [[goal]]An investor wants the upside of an asset, with protection against a fall. There are two ways to do it. [[fid]]Portfolio one: buy a call with exercise price X, and a risk-free bond that pays X at maturity. This is a fiduciary call. [[fidsum]]If the price ends below X, the call is worthless and the bond pays X. Above X, the call adds S sub T minus X, for a total of S sub T. [[pp]]Portfolio two: buy the asset, and a put with the same exercise price. This is a protective put. [[ppsum]]Below X, the put tops the asset up to X. Above X, you simply hold the asset, worth S sub T. [[same]]Both portfolios pay the larger of S sub T and X. Identical payoffs.
beats.table: [[head]]Check every scenario at maturity. [[low]]If the put is exercised, both portfolios are worth X. [[mid]]If S sub T equals X, both are worth X. [[high]]If the call is exercised, both are worth S sub T. [[rule]]Identical cash flows must have the same price today. That is put-call parity: the spot price plus the put equals the call plus the present value of X.
beats.parity: [[ex]]Back to the Viswan Family Office and its Biomian shares at two hundred ninety-five rupees. A six-month call with an exercise price of two sixty-five trades at fifty-nine. The rate is four percent. [[bond]]The bond paying two sixty-five in six months is worth two fifty-nine eighty-five today. [[solve]]So two ninety-five plus the put must equal fifty-nine plus two fifty-nine eighty-five. [[ans]]The put should cost twenty-three rupees eighty-five.
beats.arb: [[mis]]Suppose the put trades at thirty instead. Now the protective put side costs more than the fiduciary call side. [[trade]]So sell the expensive side: sell the shares and sell the put. And buy the cheap side: the call and the bond. [[cash]]Today, V F O collects two ninety-five plus thirty, minus fifty-nine, minus two fifty-nine eighty-five: six rupees fifteen. [[zero]]At maturity, the positions cancel in every scenario. The six fifteen is a riskless profit.
beats.synth: [[head]]Rearranging parity lets us build any position from the other three. [[put]]A put equals a long call, plus a long bond, minus the underlying. [[stock]]The underlying equals a long call, minus a put, plus a bond. [[tab]]Each position can be replicated with the other three: long the ones on the same side of the equation, short the ones on the other.
beats.covered: [[head]]V F O also wants income from its shares. It considers a covered call: hold the shares and sell a call with an exercise price of three twenty-five. [[eq]]From parity, the shares minus the call equal the bond minus the put. A covered call behaves like a risk-free bond plus a short put. [[pay]]Its payoff is the smaller of S sub T and X. [[ans]]With the put at fifty-six, the bond worth three eighteen sixty-nine, and the shares at two ninety-five, the call should be worth thirty-two rupees thirty-one.
beats.fwdparity: [[head]]We can also replace the shares with a forward plus a bond. [[eq]]Put-call forward parity: the present value of the forward price, plus the put, equals the call plus the present value of X. [[rearr]]Rearranged: the put minus the call equals the present value of X minus the forward price. [[ex]]The Biomian forward price is two ninety-five grown at four percent for half a year: three hundred point eight four. [[ans]]So the put is fifty-nine plus the discounted difference, two sixty-five minus three hundred point eight four. Again, twenty-three rupees eighty-five.
beats.firm: [[head]]Put-call parity also describes a company. A firm worth V has zero-coupon debt with face value D. [[solv]]At maturity, if the firm is worth more than D, debtholders get D, and shareholders keep the rest. [[insolv]]If it is worth less, debtholders take the whole firm, and shareholders get nothing. [[eq]]So equity pays the maximum of zero and V minus D: a call option on the firm's assets. [[debt]]Debt pays the minimum of V and D: a risk-free bond, minus a put sold to the shareholders. [[val]]Firm value equals the call, plus the present value of D, minus the put. [[spread]]That put is the credit risk premium. The more likely insolvency, the more valuable the put, and the riskier the debt.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]A fiduciary call and a protective put both pay the larger of S sub T and X. [[w2]]So S sub zero plus p sub zero equals c sub zero plus the present value of X; any mispricing is an arbitrage. [[w3]]Rearranged, parity replicates any one position with the other three, including covered calls and forwards. [[w4]]Equity is a call on firm value; risky debt is a bond minus a put.
beats.finish: That's the end of learning module nine.
